<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="query" aria-labelledby="_R_l9deehkd74t9_"><a href="#query" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: query()"></a><span id="_R_l9deehkd74t9_" class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>query()</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Creates a new session for each interaction with Claude Code by default. Returns an async iterator that yields messages as they arrive. See <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/sessions" class="link">Sessions</a>.</span>

<h4 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="toolannotations" aria-labelledby="_R_1v9deehkd74t9_"><a href="#toolannotations" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: ToolAnnotations"></a><span id="_R_1v9deehkd74t9_" class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>ToolAnnotations</code></span></h4>
<span data-as="p">Behavioral hints for a tool, passed as the <code>annotations</code> argument of <a href="#tool" class="link"><code>tool()</code></a>. <code>ToolAnnotations</code> extends the MCP SDK’s <code>mcp.types.ToolAnnotations</code> with a <code>maxResultSizeChars</code> field, and you can write each hint in camelCase or snake_case: <code>ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True)</code> and <code>ToolAnnotations(read_only_hint=True)</code> are equivalent. To read a hint back from the object, use the spelling your installed <code>mcp</code> package declares: <code>.readOnlyHint</code> on <code>mcp</code> 1.x and <code>.read_only_hint</code> on 2.x, while <code>.maxResultSizeChars</code> works on both. You can also pass a plain <code>mcp.types.ToolAnnotations</code> wherever the SDK accepts annotations.</span>
<span data-as="p">The snake_case names and the typed <code>maxResultSizeChars</code> field require Python Agent SDK 0.2.140 or later. Versions 0.1.31 through 0.2.139 re-export <code>mcp.types.ToolAnnotations</code> unchanged. On versions 0.1.55 through 0.2.139 you can still pass <code>maxResultSizeChars</code> as a keyword argument: the MCP class accepts extra fields, and the SDK forwards the value to Claude Code.</span>
<span data-as="p">All fields are optional. Clients shouldn’t rely on the hints for security decisions.</span>

When omitted, searches all project directories</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>up_to_message_id</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>str | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Copy the transcript up to and including the message with this UUID, such as a <code>uuid</code> from <a href="#get_session_messages" class="link"><code>get_session_messages()</code></a>. When omitted, copies the whole transcript</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>title</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>str | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Title for the fork. When omitted, the SDK derives one from the original session, followed by <code>(fork)</code></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>
<span data-as="p">Returns a <code>ForkSessionResult</code> whose <code>session_id</code> is the new session’s UUID. Pass it as <a href="#claudeagentoptions" class="link"><code>resume</code></a> to continue the fork. The fork doesn’t include the original session’s <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing" class="link">file checkpoints</a>, so you can’t rewind it to a checkpoint captured before the fork.</span>
<span data-as="p"><code>fork_session()</code> raises:</span>
<ul>
<li><code>ValueError</code>: <code>session_id</code> or <code>up_to_message_id</code> is not a valid UUID</li>
<li><code>ValueError</code>: the session has no messages, or <code>up_to_message_id</code> matches no message in the transcript</li>
<li><code>FileNotFoundError</code>: the session cannot be found</li>
</ul>

<h4 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="example-streaming-input-with-claudesdkclient" aria-labelledby="_R_779deehkd74t9_"><a href="#example-streaming-input-with-claudesdkclient" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Example - Streaming input with ClaudeSDKClient"></a><span id="_R_779deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Example - Streaming input with ClaudeSDKClient</span></h4>
<span data-as="p"><code>query()</code> also accepts an async iterable of user message dicts, so you can assemble the prompt at send time or include content blocks such as images. Claude Code starts responding to the first yielded message as soon as it arrives, without waiting for the iterable to finish, and <code>receive_response()</code> stops at the <code>ResultMessage</code> that ends that response. Put everything Claude should read before answering into one message, as this generator does, and pair each <code>query()</code> call with its own <code>receive_response()</code> loop.</span>

[&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p"><strong>Buffer behavior after interrupt:</strong> <code>interrupt()</code> sends a stop signal but does not clear the message buffer. Messages already produced by the interrupted task, including its <code>ResultMessage</code>, remain in the stream. You must drain them with <code>receive_response()</code> before reading the response to a new query. If you send a new query immediately after <code>interrupt()</code> and call <code>receive_response()</code> only once, you’ll receive the interrupted task’s messages, not the new query’s response.</span></div></div>

[&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p"><strong><code>@dataclass</code> vs <code>TypedDict</code>:</strong> This SDK uses two kinds of types. Classes decorated with <code>@dataclass</code> (such as <code>ResultMessage</code>, <code>AgentDefinition</code>, <code>TextBlock</code>) are object instances at runtime and support attribute access: <code>msg.result</code>. Classes defined with <code>TypedDict</code> (such as <code>ThinkingConfigEnabled</code>, <code>McpStdioServerConfig</code>, <code>SyncHookJSONOutput</code>) are <strong>plain dicts at runtime</strong> and require key access: <code>config[&quot;budget_tokens&quot;]</code>, not <code>config.budget_tokens</code>. The <code>ClassName(field=value)</code> call syntax works for both, but only dataclasses produce objects with attributes.</span></div></div>

See <a href="#systempromptpreset" class="link"><code>SystemPromptPreset</code></a>, <a href="#systempromptcustom" class="link"><code>SystemPromptCustom</code></a>, and <a href="#systempromptfile" class="link"><code>SystemPromptFile</code></a></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>mcp_servers</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>dict[str, McpServerConfig] | str | Path</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>{}</code></td><td style="text-align:left">MCP server configurations or path to config file</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>strict_mcp_config</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>bool</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>False</code></td><td style="text-align:left">When <code>True</code>, use the servers passed in <code>mcp_servers</code> and ignore project <code>.mcp.json</code>, user settings, plugin-provided MCP servers, and <a href="/docs/en/mcp#use-mcp-servers-from-claude-ai" class="link">claude.ai connectors</a>. Maps to the CLI <code>--strict-mcp-config</code> flag</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>permission_mode</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>PermissionMode | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Permission mode for tool usage</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>continue_conversation</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>bool</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>False</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Continue the most recent conversation</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>resume</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>str | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Session ID to resume</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>session_id</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>str | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Use a specific session ID instead of an auto-generated one. The estimate can pass this value, so <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#budget-headroom" class="link">leave headroom</a>. Counts only the call’s own spend; totals restored from a resumed session don’t count. For accuracy caveats and reset behavior, see <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking" class="link">Track cost and usage</a></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>disallowed_tools</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>list[str]</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>[]</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Tools to deny. A bare name such as <code>&quot;Bash&quot;</code> removes the tool from Claude’s context. A scoped rule such as <code>&quot;Bash(rm *)&quot;</code> leaves the tool available and denies matching calls in every permission mode, including <code>bypassPermissions</code>, for the command <a href="/docs/en/permissions#bash-rule-limits" class="link">as written</a>. See <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#allow-and-deny-rules" class="link">Permissions</a></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>enable_file_checkpointing</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>bool</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>False</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Enable file change tracking for rewinding. Accepts a comma-separated list. For guidance, see <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/configuration#choose-a-model" class="link">Choose a model</a></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>betas</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>list[SdkBeta]</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>[]</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Beta features to enable. See <a href="#sdkbeta" class="link"><code>SdkBeta</code></a> for available options</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>output_format</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>dict[str, Any] | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Output format for structured responses (e.g., <code>{&quot;type&quot;: &quot;json_schema&quot;, &quot;schema&quot;: {...}}</code>). See <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/structured-outputs" class="link">Structured outputs</a> for details</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>permission_prompt_tool_name</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>str | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">MCP tool name for permission prompts</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>cwd</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>str | Path | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Current working directory</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>cli_path</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>str | Path | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Custom path to the Claude Code CLI executable</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>settings</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>str | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Path to a settings file or an inline JSON string</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>add_dirs</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>list[str | Path]</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>[]</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Additional directories Claude can access. The SDK passes each entry to Claude Code as <code>--add-dir</code>, so with the <code>project</code> setting source Claude Code also <a href="/docs/en/permissions#additional-directories-grant-file-access-not-configuration" class="link">loads the directory’s skills, commands, and subagents</a></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>env</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>dict[str, str]</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>{}</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Environment variables merged on top of the inherited process environment. See <a href="/docs/en/env-vars" class="link">Environment variables</a> for variables the underlying CLI reads, and <a href="#handle-slow-or-stalled-api-responses" class="link">Handle slow or stalled API responses</a> for timeout-related variables. Set <code>CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_CLIENT_APP</code> to identify your app in the User-Agent header</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>extra_args</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>dict[str, str | None]</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>{}</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Additional CLI arguments to pass directly to the CLI</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>max_buffer_size</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>int | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Longest single message the SDK accepts from the CLI, in characters. <code>None</code> uses 1,048,576. A longer message raises <a href="#clijsondecodeerror" class="link"><code>CLIJSONDecodeError</code></a></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>debug_stderr</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>Any</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>sys.stderr</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><em>Deprecated</em> - The SDK ignores this value. Use the <code>stderr</code> callback for CLI stderr output</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>stderr</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>Callable[[str], None] | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Callback function for stderr output from CLI</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>can_use_tool</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><a href="#canusetool" class="link"><code>CanUseTool</code></a> <code> | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Tool permission callback, invoked only when the <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#how-permissions-are-evaluated" class="link">permission flow</a> falls through to a prompt. Not invoked for calls auto-approved by <code>allowed_tools</code>, allow rules, or <code>permission_mode</code>. An allow rule doesn’t pre-approve the <a href="/docs/en/permission-modes#actions-no-mode-auto-approves" class="link">actions no mode auto-approves</a>. See <a href="#canusetool" class="link"><code>CanUseTool</code></a> for details</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>hooks</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>dict[HookEvent, list[HookMatcher]] | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Hook configurations for intercepting events</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>user</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>str | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">On POSIX platforms, the OS user account the Claude Code subprocess runs as. Claude Code keeps the parent process’s environment, including <code>HOME</code>, and runs in <code>cwd</code></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>include_partial_messages</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>bool</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>False</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Include partial message streaming events. When enabled, <a href="#streamevent" class="link"><code>StreamEvent</code></a> messages are yielded</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>include_hook_events</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>bool</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>False</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Include hook lifecycle events in the message stream as <code>HookEventMessage</code> objects</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>forward_subagent_text</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>bool</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>False</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Forward subagent text and thinking blocks in the message stream. Without this option, Claude Code omits the text and thinking blocks of a subagent that runs in the <a href="/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background" class="link">foreground</a>. For nested subagents, skills with <code>context: fork</code>, and the Claude Code version each needs, see <a href="/docs/en/headless#follow-subagent-messages" class="link">Follow subagent messages</a>. Requires Python Agent SDK 0.2.140 or later</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>verbatim_prompts</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>bool</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>False</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Deliver every prompt as written. The SDK sends each user message with <code>client_composed</code> set to <code>True</code>. See <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkusermessage" class="link"><code>client_composed</code></a> for what Claude Code skips on those messages. Use this option when your prompt text includes content the end user didn’t type. For per-turn control, leave it off and set <code>&quot;client_composed&quot;: True</code> on individual streamed messages instead. While the option is on, the SDK overwrites any <code>client_composed</code> value you set. Requires Python Agent SDK 0.2.158 or later and Claude Code v2.1.248 or later; the CLI bundled with those SDK versions satisfies the Claude Code requirement</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>fork_session</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>bool</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>False</code></td><td style="text-align:left">When resuming with <code>resume</code>, fork to a new session ID instead of continuing the original session</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>resume_session_at</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>str | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">When resuming, load the conversation only up to and including the message with this UUID. Use with <code>resume</code>, and usually <code>fork_session</code>, to branch from an earlier point. Requires Python Agent SDK 0.2.137 or later</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>resume_drops_turn</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>str | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">UUID of the user prompt whose turn a <code>resume_session_at</code> truncation discards. When set, the CLI refuses the resume if the discarded range holds entries not attributable to that turn. Requires Python Agent SDK 0.2.137 or later and Claude Code v2.1.223 or later; the CLI bundled with those SDK versions satisfies the Claude Code requirement</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>agents</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>dict[str, AgentDefinition] | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Programmatically defined subagents</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>plugins</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>list[SdkPluginConfig]</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>[]</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Load custom plugins from local paths. See <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/plugins" class="link">Plugins</a> for details</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>sandbox</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><a href="#sandboxsettings" class="link"><code>SandboxSettings</code></a> <code> | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Configure sandbox behavior programmatically. See <a href="#sandboxsettings" class="link">Sandbox settings</a> for details</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>setting_sources</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>list[SettingSource] | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code> (CLI defaults: all sources)</td><td style="text-align:left">Control which filesystem settings to load. Pass <code>[]</code> to disable user, project, and local settings. With <code>skills</code> set and this field unset, only user and project sources load. Set <code>setting_sources</code> explicitly to keep local settings. Endpoint-managed policy loads regardless; server-managed settings are fetched when the session authenticates with an organization credential on an <a href="/docs/en/server-managed-settings#platform-availability" class="link">eligible configuration</a>. For inputs read regardless of this option, see <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/claude-code-features#what-settingsources-does-not-control" class="link">What settingSources does not control</a></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>skills</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>list[str] | Literal[&quot;all&quot;] | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Limits the main agent’s skills. Pass <code>&quot;all&quot;</code> to enable every discovered skill, or a list of skill names. Pass exact names only. The SDK rejects malformed and wildcard-form names with a <code>ValueError</code> before starting the Claude Code process; this check requires Python Agent SDK 0.2.129 or later. If you also pass <code>tools</code>, include <code>&quot;Skill&quot;</code> in that list. See <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/skills" class="link">Skills</a></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>max_thinking_tokens</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>int | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><em>Deprecated</em> - Maximum tokens for thinking blocks. Use <code>thinking</code> instead</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>thinking</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><a href="#thinkingconfig" class="link"><code>ThinkingConfig</code></a> <code> | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Controls extended thinking behavior. Takes precedence over <code>max_thinking_tokens</code></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>effort</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><a href="#effortlevel" class="link"><code>EffortLevel</code></a> <code> | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Effort level for thinking depth. See <a href="/docs/en/model-config#adjust-effort-level" class="link">adjust the effort level</a></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>session_store</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#the-sessionstore-interface" class="link"><code>SessionStore</code></a> <code> | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Mirror session transcripts to an external backend so another host can resume them. See <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage" class="link">Persist sessions to external storage</a></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>session_store_flush</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>Literal[&quot;batched&quot;, &quot;eager&quot;]</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>&quot;batched&quot;</code></td><td style="text-align:left">When to flush mirrored transcript entries to <code>session_store</code>. <code>&quot;batched&quot;</code> flushes once per turn or when the buffer fills; <code>&quot;eager&quot;</code> triggers a background flush after every frame. Ignored when <code>session_store</code> is <code>None</code></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>load_timeout_ms</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>int</code></td><td data-numeric="true" style="text-align:left"><code>60000</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Per-call timeout for <code>session_store.load()</code> and <code>list_subkeys()</code> during resume materialization, in milliseconds</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>task_budget</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>TaskBudget | None</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>None</code></td><td style="text-align:left">API-side token budget. Sent as <code>output_config.task_budget</code> with the <code>task-budgets-2026-03-13</code> beta header. Pass <code>{&quot;total&quot;: &lt;int&gt;}</code>.</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>
<h4 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="handle-slow-or-stalled-api-responses" aria-labelledby="_R_8n9deehkd74t9_"><a href="#handle-slow-or-stalled-api-responses" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Handle slow or stalled API responses"></a><span id="_R_8n9deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Handle slow or stalled API responses</span></h4>

style="color:#CF222E;--shiki-dark:#C586C0">from</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4"> claude_agent_sdk </span><span style="color:#CF222E;--shiki-dark:#C586C0">import</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4"> ClaudeAgentOptions</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">options </span><span style="color:#CF222E;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">=</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4"> ClaudeAgentOptions(</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#953800;--shiki-dark:#9CDCFE">    env</span><span style="color:#CF222E;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">=</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">{</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#0A3069;--shiki-dark:#CE9178">        &quot;API_TIMEOUT_MS&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">: </span><span style="color:#0A3069;--shiki-dark:#CE9178">&quot;120000&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">,</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#0A3069;--shiki-dark:#CE9178">        &quot;CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">: </span><span style="color:#0A3069;--shiki-dark:#CE9178">&quot;2&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">,</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#0A3069;--shiki-dark:#CE9178">        &quot;CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">: </span><span style="color:#0A3069;--shiki-dark:#CE9178">&quot;120000&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">,</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">    },</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">)</span></span>
</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div class="code-block-fade-overlay print:hidden" data-fade-overlay="true" aria-hidden="true" style="--fade-color-light:#ffffff;--fade-color-dark:#0B0C0E"></div></div>
<ul>
<li>
<span data-as="p"><a href="/docs/en/env-vars" class="link"><code>API_TIMEOUT_MS</code></a>: how long each request attempt can wait for response headers, in milliseconds. It doesn’t limit how long a streaming response runs after the headers arrive. Default <code>600000</code>. Applies to the main loop and all subagents.</span>
</li>
<li>
<span data-as="p"><code>CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES</code>: maximum API retries. Default <code>10</code>, capped at <code>15</code>. Each retry gets its own <code>API_TIMEOUT_MS</code> window.</span>
<span data-as="p">For unattended runs that need to wait through longer outages, set <a href="/docs/en/errors#tune-retry-behavior" class="link"><code>CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG=1</code></a>: it retries transient capacity errors indefinitely and, on Claude Code v2.1.199 or later, raises the default for other transient errors to <code>300</code> and removes the cap on this variable.</span>
</li>
<li>
<span data-as="p"><code>CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS</code>: stall watchdog for subagents. While the stream watchdog is on, the default is <code>CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS</code> plus 5 minutes, which comes to <code>600000</code> unless you raise that variable. With the stream watchdog off, the default is <code>600000</code>. Before v2.1.257, the default was always <code>600000</code>.</span>
<span data-as="p">The timer resets on each stream event. On a stall, Claude Code aborts the subagent and reports the stall to the parent. For a background subagent, it also marks the task failed and attaches any partial result.</span>
</li>
<li>
<span data-as="p"><code>CLAUDE_ENABLE_STREAM_WATCHDOG</code> with <code>CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS</code>: stream watchdog that aborts the request when headers have arrived but the response body stops streaming. The watchdog is on by default for all providers; set <code>CLAUDE_ENABLE_STREAM_WATCHDOG=0</code> to disable it. <code>CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS</code> defaults to <code>300000</code> and is clamped to that minimum. After the abort, <a href="/docs/en/errors#automatic-retries" class="link">Automatic retries</a> covers what Claude Code does, based on how far the response had progressed.</span>
<span data-as="p">While the watchdog waits out a response that a gateway behind <code>ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL</code> holds open with keep-alive pings, a host that sets <code>include_partial_messages</code> keeps receiving <code>ping</code> <a href="#streamevent" class="link"><code>StreamEvent</code></a> messages. Read those frames as liveness rather than timing the session out on silence. Before v2.1.257, the frames stopped 5 minutes after the last real stream event.</span>
</li>

<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="systempromptfile" aria-labelledby="_R_9n9deehkd74t9_"><a href="#systempromptfile" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: SystemPromptFile"></a><span id="_R_9n9deehkd74t9_" class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>SystemPromptFile</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Configuration for loading a custom system prompt from a file instead of passing it as a string. The SDK maps this to the CLI <a href="/docs/en/cli-reference#system-prompt-flags" class="link"><code>--system-prompt-file</code></a> flag. Use the file form when the prompt is large: the SDK passes a string <code>system_prompt</code> on the CLI subprocess argv, which is subject to OS command-line length limits before the SDK sends any API request. On Linux a single argument longer than roughly 128 KB fails at process spawn with <code>Argument list too long</code>. On Windows the whole command line is capped at roughly 32 KB, so the string form fails at a lower threshold.</span>

<h4 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="default-behavior" aria-labelledby="_R_a79deehkd74t9_"><a href="#default-behavior" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Default behavior"></a><span id="_R_a79deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Default behavior</span></h4>
<span data-as="p">When <code>setting_sources</code> is omitted or <code>None</code> and <code>skills</code> is not set, <code>query()</code> loads the same filesystem settings as the Claude Code CLI: user, project, and local. With <code>skills</code> set, the <a href="#claudeagentoptions" class="link"><code>setting_sources</code></a> row describes the current default. Endpoint-managed policy is loaded in all cases; server-managed settings are fetched when the session authenticates with an organization credential on an <a href="/docs/en/server-managed-settings#platform-availability" class="link">eligible configuration</a>. For more information, see <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/claude-code-features#what-settingsources-does-not-control" class="link">What settingSources does not control</a>.</span>

<span data-as="p">To load CLAUDE.md project instructions, include <code>&quot;project&quot;</code> in <code>setting_sources</code>. See <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts#claude-md-files-for-project-level-instructions" class="link">Modify system prompts</a> for how CLAUDE.md loading interacts with the system prompt options.</span>
<h4 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="settings-precedence" aria-labelledby="_R_at9deehkd74t9_"><a href="#settings-precedence" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Settings precedence"></a><span id="_R_at9deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Settings precedence</span></h4>
<span data-as="p">When multiple sources are loaded, settings are merged with this precedence (highest to lowest):</span>
<ol>
<li>Local settings (<code>.claude/settings.local.json</code>)</li>
<li>Project settings (<code>.claude/settings.json</code>)</li>
<li>User settings (<code>~/.claude/settings.json</code>)</li>
</ol>

[&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p"><code>AgentDefinition</code> field names use camelCase, such as <code>disallowedTools</code>, <code>permissionMode</code>, and <code>maxTurns</code>. These names map directly to the wire format shared with the TypeScript SDK. This differs from <code>ClaudeAgentOptions</code>, which uses Python snake_case for the equivalent top-level fields such as <code>disallowed_tools</code> and <code>permission_mode</code>. Because <code>AgentDefinition</code> is a dataclass, passing a snake_case keyword raises a <code>TypeError</code> at construction time.</span></div></div>

<span data-as="p">The callback receives:</span>
<ul>
<li><code>tool_name</code>: Name of the tool being called</li>
<li><code>input_data</code>: The tool’s input parameters</li>
<li><code>context</code>: A <code>ToolPermissionContext</code> with additional information</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">Returns a <code>PermissionResult</code> (either <code>PermissionResultAllow</code> or <code>PermissionResultDeny</code>).</span>
<span data-as="p">The callback replaces the interactive permission prompt. The SDK calls <code>can_use_tool</code> when the <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#how-permissions-are-evaluated" class="link">permission evaluation flow</a> resolves to a prompt. Calls approved in either of these ways run without calling <code>can_use_tool</code>:</span>
<ul>
<li>A call that an <code>allowed_tools</code> entry or a settings allow rule approves</li>
<li>A call the permission mode approves, such as a file edit in <code>acceptEdits</code> mode</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">To check those calls, use a <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks" class="link"><code>PreToolUse</code> hook</a>, which runs for them too.</span>
<span data-as="p">An allow rule doesn’t pre-approve the <a href="/docs/en/permission-modes#actions-no-mode-auto-approves" class="link">actions no mode auto-approves</a>; see <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#how-permissions-are-evaluated" class="link">How permissions are evaluated</a> for which of them reach the callback and what happens in <code>dontAsk</code> and <code>auto</code> mode.</span>

<span data-as="p">If you return <code>PermissionResultAllow</code> with more than 4,096 items in <code>updated_permissions</code>, Claude Code treats the result as invalid and denies the tool call. Each <a href="#permissionupdate" class="link"><code>PermissionUpdate</code></a> counts as one item, and so does each entry in its <code>rules</code> or <code>directories</code> list. The denial message ends with <code>updatedPermissions may hold at most 4096 updates, rules and directories in all.</code> To avoid the denial, return 4,096 items or fewer.</span>

<span data-as="p">The optional <code>display</code> field controls whether thinking text is returned <code>&quot;summarized&quot;</code> or <code>&quot;omitted&quot;</code>. On Claude Opus 4.7 and later, the API default is <code>&quot;omitted&quot;</code>, so set <code>&quot;summarized&quot;</code> to receive thinking content in <a href="#thinkingblock" class="link"><code>ThinkingBlock</code></a> outputs. On providers such as Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, Claude Code doesn’t pass <code>display</code> for earlier models it recognizes. Those are Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5, and earlier models, which use their default.</span>
<span data-as="p">Because these are <code>TypedDict</code> classes, they’re plain dicts at runtime. Either construct them as dict literals or call the class like a constructor; both produce a <code>dict</code>. Access fields with <code>config[&quot;budget_tokens&quot;]</code>, not <code>config.budget_tokens</code>:</span>

<div role="note" aria-label="Warning" class="callout my-4 px-5 py-4 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl flex gap-3 border border-yellow-200 bg-yellow-50 dark:border-yellow-900 dark:bg-yellow-600/20 [&amp;_[data-component-part=&#x27;callout-icon&#x27;]]:mt-px" data-callout-type="warning"><div class="mt-0.5 w-4" data-component-part="callout-icon"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="1.5" class="flex-none size-5 text-yellow-800 dark:text-yellow-300"><use href="#mi-mint-1-CalloutWarning"></use></svg></div><div class="text-sm prose dark:prose-invert min-w-0 w-full [&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-light dark:[&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-dark [&amp;_code]:text-current! [&amp;_kbd]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-yellow-800 dark:text-yellow-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p">On the Claude API, the <code>context-1m-2025-08-07</code> beta is retired for Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Claude Sonnet 4. If you still pass it with either model, requests that exceed the standard 200K-token context window return an error, so remove it from <code>betas</code>. To run a session with a 1M-token context window, set <code>model</code> to a model that <a href="/docs/en/model-config#extended-context" class="link">runs with the 1M window by default</a>, such as <code>claude-sonnet-5-5</code> or <code>claude-opus-5-5</code>. For a model that reaches 1M only through its <code>[1m]</code> variant, append the suffix to the model ID, as in <code>claude-opus-4-6[1m]</code>.</span></div></div>

<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="contextusageresponse" aria-labelledby="_R_gj9deehkd74t9_"><a href="#contextusageresponse" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: ContextUsageResponse"></a><span id="_R_gj9deehkd74t9_" class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>ContextUsageResponse</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Response from <a href="#methods" class="link"><code>ClaudeSDKClient.get_context_usage()</code></a>. The response includes the payload Claude Code renders for the <code>/context</code> command in an interactive session. Alongside the token counts, that payload carries display fields such as <code>color</code> and <code>gridRows</code> that Claude Code uses to draw the <code>/context</code> usage grid.</span>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code builds this payload by sending several requests to the <a href="https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/token-counting" class="link" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">token-counting</a> API. These requests don’t appear in the message stream, so cost tracking that reads the stream won’t see them. On the Anthropic API, token counting isn’t billed.</span>

<span data-as="p">Each <code>ContextUsageCategory</code> entry carries <code>name</code>, <code>tokens</code>, <code>color</code>, and an optional <code>isDeferred</code> flag. <code>totalTokens</code> is the session’s current context usage, and <code>maxTokens</code> is the window that usage is measured against. That window is the model’s context window, or the lower auto-compaction window when one applies, and <code>rawMaxTokens</code> carries the same value as <code>maxTokens</code>. <code>apiUsage</code> holds the usage from the latest API response, not a running total for the session. Claude Code leaves the optional <code>deferredBuiltinTools</code>, <code>systemTools</code>, and <code>systemPromptSections</code> keys unset, so expect them to be absent even though the type declares them.</span>

Requires Python Agent SDK 0.2.137 or later</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>
<span data-as="p">The SDK passes <code>tool_use_result</code> through from the CLI unmodified. For a tool on an external MCP server whose result contains <code>resource_link</code> blocks, the dict has a <code>resourceLinks</code> key holding a list of dicts with the keys of the TypeScript <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkmcpresourcelink" class="link"><code>SDKMcpResourceLink</code></a> type. Claude receives each link as a line of text in the tool result. To render the files the server returned, read <code>resourceLinks</code> instead of parsing that text. The <code>resourceLinks</code> key requires Python Agent SDK 0.2.150 or later and Claude Code v2.1.257 or later; the CLI bundled with that SDK version satisfies the Claude Code requirement.</span>
<span data-as="p">The CLI omits the key when the result has no links and on results from subagents. The CLI keeps at most 50 links per result and stops adding links once the list reaches 64 KiB of serialized JSON. A tool you define in-process with <a href="#tool" class="link"><code>tool()</code></a> never produces the key, because the SDK flattens its <code>resource_link</code> blocks to text before the CLI sees the result.</span>

<span data-as="p">Subtypes that have no dataclass of their own arrive as <code>SystemMessage</code>. To follow the session between turns, set <a href="/docs/en/env-vars#variables" class="link"><code>CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_SESSION_STATE_EVENTS=1</code></a> and read <code>message.data[&quot;state&quot;]</code> on each message whose <code>subtype</code> is <code>session_state_changed</code>. <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdksessionstatechangedmessage" class="link"><code>SDKSessionStateChangedMessage</code></a> lists the states it can carry. Iterate with <code>receive_messages()</code> to read them: <code>receive_response()</code> stops at the <code>ResultMessage</code>, and a <code>session_state_changed</code> message can follow that result.</span>

<span data-as="p">The <code>subtype</code> field determines which other fields are populated. It is one of <code>&quot;success&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;error_during_execution&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;error_max_turns&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;error_max_budget_usd&quot;</code>, or <code>&quot;error_max_structured_output_retries&quot;</code>. The Python dataclass flattens all variants into one shape, so fields that don’t apply to the returned subtype are <code>None</code>.</span>
<span data-as="p">Several fields carry diagnostic detail about how the conversation ended:</span>
<ul>
<li><code>is_error</code>: <code>True</code> when the conversation ended in an error state. Always <code>True</code> on the <code>error_*</code> subtypes. On <code>subtype=&quot;success&quot;</code> it is <code>True</code> in three cases. Check <code>stop_reason</code> to tell them apart:<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>&quot;refusal&quot;</code>: the model declined to respond. Read the refusal text in <code>result</code>, or in the preceding <code>AssistantMessage</code> when <code>result</code> is empty.</li>
<li><code>&quot;tool_deferred_unavailable&quot;</code>: the <a href="/docs/en/hooks#defer-a-tool-call-for-later" class="link">deferred tool</a> was no longer available when you resumed the session, for example because its MCP server wasn’t connected. In the two cases below, a prompt you send after resuming counts the same as one passed with the resume:<!-- -->
<ul>
<li>No prompt: by default, the call is still pending. Make the tool available and resume again without a prompt, and the call runs first.</li>
<li>A prompt: by default, the prompt doesn’t reach Claude and the call is still pending. To continue without the tool, <a href="/docs/en/hooks#resume-when-a-deferred-tool-is-unavailable" class="link">drop the call</a>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Any other value: the turn ended on an error that Claude Code reported in place of a model response, such as an API error. Read <code>terminal_reason</code> for the cause, <code>result</code> for the message, and <code>api_error_status</code> for the HTTP status when the API returned one.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><code>api_error_status</code>: the HTTP status code of the terminating API error. <code>None</code> when the turn ended without one. Populated only on <code>subtype=&quot;success&quot;</code>.</li>
<li><code>result</code>: text of the final assistant message on <code>subtype=&quot;success&quot;</code>, or <code>None</code> on the <code>error_*</code> subtypes. When <code>subtype=&quot;success&quot;</code> and <code>is_error=True</code>, this holds the API error string if one is available but can be empty, so check <code>api_error_status</code> and the preceding <code>AssistantMessage</code> content for detail.</li>
<li><code>errors</code>: loop-level error strings such as the max-turns message. Populated only on the <code>error_*</code> subtypes.</li>
<li><code>terminal_reason</code>: why the query loop ended, such as <code>&quot;completed&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;max_turns&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;api_error&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;aborted_streaming&quot;</code>, or <code>&quot;aborted_tools&quot;</code>. A value of <code>&quot;aborted_streaming&quot;</code> or <code>&quot;aborted_tools&quot;</code> means the turn was aborted before completing. Common causes are <a href="#claudesdkclient" class="link"><code>interrupt()</code></a> and a permission callback returning <a href="#permissionresultdeny" class="link"><code>PermissionResultDeny</code></a> with <code>interrupt=True</code>. <code>None</code> on CLI versions that predate the field, on results from local commands such as <code>/voice</code> or <code>/usage</code>, which bypass the query loop, or on synthesized error results emitted when the session fails fatally. Mirrors the TypeScript SDK’s <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkresultmessage" class="link"><code>SDKResultMessage.terminal_reason</code></a>, which lists the full set of values.</li>
<li><code>origin</code>: origin of the user message that triggered this turn. Requires Python Agent SDK 0.2.137 or later. Don’t suppress a result on <code>kind</code> alone. In <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/streaming-vs-single-mode" class="link">streaming input mode</a>, check <code>origin</code> to see whether your own prompt started the turn:<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><strong>Your own prompt</strong>: <code>origin</code> is <code>None</code> or <code>{&quot;kind&quot;: &quot;human&quot;}</code></li>
<li><strong>A background-task notification</strong>: <code>origin[&quot;kind&quot;]</code> is <code>&quot;task-notification&quot;</code>. That turn’s result can also hold Claude’s answer to a message you sent while the turn ran tools.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">When several background tasks finish close together, Claude Code can answer their notifications in one turn rather than one turn each. You still receive one <code>ResultMessage</code> per notification, in order, each with an <code>origin</code> whose <code>kind</code> is <code>&quot;task-notification&quot;</code>. All but the last have <code>num_turns</code> set to <code>0</code> and an empty <code>result</code>, and the last one carries the turn that answers them all.</span>
<span data-as="p">The <code>usage</code> dict covers the main agent loop only and excludes subagent and other nested or auxiliary model calls. In <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/streaming-vs-single-mode" class="link">streaming input mode</a>, the values are per-turn. Prefer <code>model_usage</code> for token and cost accounting. The <code>usage</code> dict contains the following keys when present:</span>
<!-- --><div role="presentation" style="position:relative;--scroll-area-corner-height:0px;--scroll-area-corner-width:0px" data-component-part="scroll-area" data-table-wrapper="true" class="min-w-0 [--page-padding:20px] flex w-[calc(100%+(var(--page-padding)*2))] my-[1em] py-[1em] -mx-(--page-padding) max-w-none [contain:inline-size]"><div data-id="base-ui-_R_j79deehkd74t9_-viewport" tabindex="-1" class="size-full rounded-[inherit] [--scroll-area-fade-size:32px] overflow-y-hidden! base-ui-disable-scrollbar" style="overflow:scroll" data-component-part="scroll-area-viewport" role="region" aria-label="Scrollable table"><div role="presentation" style="min-width:fit-content" data-component-part="scroll-area-content" class="flex"><div class="px-(--page-padding) grow max-w-none table"><table class="m-0 min-w-full w-full max-w-none table [&amp;_th]:text-left [&amp;_td[data-numeric]]:tabular-nums [&amp;_td]:min-w-[150px]"><thead><tr><th>Key</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>input_tokens</code></td><td><code>int</code></td><td>Input tokens consumed by the top-level agent loop. <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#get-the-total-cost-of-a-query" class="link">Subagent tokens aren’t included</a>; use <code>model_usage</code> for whole-tree accounting.</td></tr><tr><td><code>output_tokens</code></td><td><code>int</code></td><td>Output tokens generated by the top-level agent loop. Subagent tokens aren’t included.</td></tr><tr><td><code>cache_creation_input_tokens</code></td><td><code>int</code></td><td>Tokens used to create new cache entries.</td></tr><tr><td><code>cache_read_input_tokens</code></td><td><code>int</code></td><td>Tokens read from existing cache entries.</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>
<span data-as="p">The <code>model_usage</code> dict maps model names to per-model usage. It covers every model call made through the query pipeline: the main loop, subagents, and internal calls such as compaction and Workflow agents. Helper calls outside that pipeline, such as the permission classifier and token-counting requests, are excluded from <code>model_usage</code>. Treat <code>model_usage</code> as an estimate, not a billing statement.</span>
<span data-as="p">In <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/streaming-vs-single-mode" class="link">streaming input mode</a>, <code>model_usage</code> and <code>total_cost_usd</code> are cumulative across turns, so read the latest result rather than summing across results. A call that resumes a session also counts the <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#accumulate-costs-across-multiple-calls" class="link">totals restored from the session’s earlier calls</a>. See <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#track-costs-in-streaming-input-mode" class="link">Track costs in streaming input mode</a> for resets and <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#recover-totals-after-a-session-crash" class="link">Recover totals after a session crash</a> for zeroed results.</span>
<span data-as="p">Each value in <code>model_usage</code> is a <code>ModelUsage</code> TypedDict, imported via <code>from claude_agent_sdk.types import ModelUsage</code>. Its keys use camelCase because the SDK passes the value through unmodified from the underlying CLI process, matching the TypeScript <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#modelusage" class="link"><code>ModelUsage</code></a> type:</span>

Absent until a turn runs on a Claude Code version that records it, and not declared on the TypedDict, so read it with <code>.get()</code>. Requires Python Agent SDK 0.2.150 or later, whose bundled CLI records it.</td></tr><tr><td><code>costUSD</code></td><td><code>float</code></td><td>Estimated cost in USD for this model, computed client-side. See <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking" class="link">Track cost and usage</a> for billing caveats.</td></tr><tr><td><code>contextWindow</code></td><td><code>int</code></td><td>Context window size for this model.</td></tr><tr><td><code>maxOutputTokens</code></td><td><code>int</code></td><td>Maximum output token limit for this model.</td></tr><tr><td><code>canonicalModel</code></td><td><code>str</code></td><td>Canonical model ID used for the pricing lookup. May differ from the raw model string the entry is keyed by, such as a provider-specific ID or alias. Not always present.</td></tr><tr><td><code>provider</code></td><td><code>str</code></td><td>API provider that served this model, such as <code>firstParty</code>, <code>bedrock</code>, <code>vertex</code>, <code>foundry</code>, <code>anthropicAws</code>, <code>mantle</code>, or <code>gateway</code>. Not always present.</td></tr><tr><td><code>costBasis</code></td><td><code>str</code></td><td>Price table that priced this model’s latest request: <code>list</code> for list price, <code>managed</code> for a <a href="/docs/en/settings-reference#modelpricing" class="link"><code>modelPricing</code></a> table, or <code>unknown</code> when neither matched the model ID. Not always present, and not declared on the TypedDict, so read it with <code>.get()</code>. Requires Claude Code v2.1.246 or later.</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>

<span data-as="p">When the CLI <a href="/docs/en/mcp#automatic-backgrounding-of-long-tool-calls" class="link">moves a long MCP tool call to the background</a>, the tool result for that call holds only a placeholder and the call’s real result arrives in this message. On a <code>&quot;completed&quot;</code> notification for such a call, the CLI adds a <code>resource_links</code> key listing the files the tool returned by reference, with the same entries and limits as the <code>resourceLinks</code> key on <a href="#usermessage" class="link"><code>UserMessage.tool_use_result</code></a>. The <code>resource_links</code> key requires Python Agent SDK 0.2.150 or later and Claude Code v2.1.257 or later; the CLI bundled with that SDK version satisfies the Claude Code requirement.</span>
<span data-as="p">The dataclass has no field for <code>resource_links</code>. Read it from the <code>data</code> dict the message inherits from <a href="#systemmessage" class="link"><code>SystemMessage</code></a>: <code>message.data.get(&quot;resource_links&quot;)</code>. Match the notification to the call with <code>tool_use_id</code>. The CLI omits the key when the result had no links and on notifications for tasks that aren’t MCP tool calls.</span>

<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="resulterror" aria-labelledby="_R_nh9deehkd74t9_"><a href="#resulterror" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: ResultError"></a><span id="_R_nh9deehkd74t9_" class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>ResultError</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Raised when the Claude Code process exits because the run ended with an error <a href="#resultmessage" class="link">result message</a>, such as a turn-limit error or an API error. <code>ResultError</code> subclasses <code>ProcessError</code>, so an existing <code>except ProcessError</code> handler also catches it. Its attributes carry the fields of that result message, so you can branch on why the run failed without parsing the message text. Requires Python Agent SDK 0.2.140 or later.</span>

<span data-as="p">To tell failures apart, check <code>data[&quot;stop_reason&quot;]</code> first, then <code>terminal_reason</code>, then <code>subtype</code>. A declined response has <code>stop_reason</code> <code>&quot;refusal&quot;</code>, usually with <code>subtype</code> <code>&quot;success&quot;</code>; its <code>terminal_reason</code> doesn’t single it out and can read <code>&quot;completed&quot;</code> or <code>&quot;api_error&quot;</code>. A failed final request has <code>subtype</code> <code>&quot;success&quot;</code> and its cause in <code>terminal_reason</code>, such as <code>&quot;api_error&quot;</code> for an API error. When the run hits a limit you set, such as <code>max_turns</code> or <code>max_budget_usd</code>, you get an <code>error_*</code> subtype.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="clijsondecodeerror" aria-labelledby="_R_np9deehkd74t9_"><a href="#clijsondecodeerror" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: CLIJSONDecodeError"></a><span id="_R_np9deehkd74t9_" class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>CLIJSONDecodeError</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Raised when JSON parsing fails, or when one message from the CLI is longer than <code>max_buffer_size</code>. To raise the limit and pick up the stopped work, see <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/troubleshooting#large-tool-calls-and-results" class="link">Large tool calls and results</a>.</span>

<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="hook-usage-example" aria-labelledby="_R_sv9deehkd74t9_"><a href="#hook-usage-example" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Hook Usage Example"></a><span id="_R_sv9deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Hook Usage Example</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">This example registers two hooks: one that blocks dangerous Bash commands like <code>rm -rf /</code>, and another that logs all tool usage for auditing. With its <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#matchers" class="link"><code>Bash</code> matcher</a>, the security hook runs on Bash tool calls. The logging hook has no matcher, so it matches every tool.</span>

<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="tool-input/output-types" aria-labelledby="_R_t59deehkd74t9_"><a href="#tool-input/output-types" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Tool Input/Output Types"></a><span id="_R_t59deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Tool Input/Output Types</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">Documentation of input/output schemas for built-in Claude Code tools. While the Python SDK doesn’t export these as types, they represent the structure of tool inputs and outputs in messages.</span>
<span data-as="p">Each output shown is the value you read from <a href="#usermessage" class="link"><code>UserMessage.tool_use_result</code></a> for that tool. Key names appear exactly as Claude Code emits them. A key annotated <code>| None</code> with a “present when” or “optional” comment is omitted when it doesn’t apply.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="agent" aria-labelledby="_R_tb9deehkd74t9_"><a href="#agent" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Agent"></a><span id="_R_tb9deehkd74t9_" class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer">Agent</span></h3>
<span data-as="p"><strong>Tool name:</strong> <code>Agent</code>. The previous name <code>Task</code> is still accepted as an alias when this tool is available to the session.</span>
<span data-as="p">The <code>tools</code> list in the init <a href="#systemmessage" class="link"><code>SystemMessage</code></a> reports this tool as <code>Task</code> for backward compatibility.</span>

<span data-as="p">Launches a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously.</span>
<span data-as="p">When Claude leaves <code>run_in_background</code> out of an <code>Agent</code> call, by default your main agent doesn’t wait for the new agent and a subagent waits:</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>From your main agent</strong>: the new agent runs in the background, and the result has <code>status: &quot;async_launched&quot;</code>. To make your main agent wait for the new agent instead, see <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents#choose-whether-claude-waits-for-subagents" class="link">Choose whether Claude waits for subagents</a>.</li>
<li><strong>From one of your subagents</strong>: the calling subagent <a href="/docs/en/sub-agents#let-subagents-spawn-their-own-subagents" class="link">waits for the new agent</a>. The new agent runs in the background instead when its definition sets <a href="#agentdefinition" class="link"><code>background</code></a> to <code>True</code>.</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">Before Python SDK v0.2.169, agents that your subagents started also ran in the background by default. That release is the first to bundle Claude Code v2.1.302 or later.</span>

<span data-as="p">Returns the result from the subagent. The output is discriminated on the <code>status</code> field: <code>&quot;completed&quot;</code> for finished tasks, <code>&quot;async_launched&quot;</code> for background tasks, and <code>&quot;remote_launched&quot;</code> for tasks Claude Code dispatched to a cloud session, where <code>sessionUrl</code> links to that session and <code>taskId</code> identifies it. If Claude Code <a href="/docs/en/worktrees#isolate-subagents-with-worktrees" class="link">kept the subagent’s isolated worktree</a>, <code>worktreePath</code> on the <code>completed</code> variant is where to find it, and <code>worktreeBranch</code> is its branch when Claude Code created the worktree with git.</span>
<span data-as="p">On the <code>completed</code> variant, <code>resolvedModel</code> names the model the subagent started on, which can differ from the requested <code>model</code> input when <a href="/docs/en/model-config#restrict-model-selection" class="link"><code>availableModels</code></a> or another override applies. This field requires Claude Code v2.1.174 or later. On the <code>async_launched</code> variant, <code>resolvedModel</code> names the model in use when the agent moved to the background, so a swap that happened before backgrounding is reflected there. The <code>modelsUsed</code> field on both variants lists the models used in order, with consecutive repeats collapsed; it’s set only when the model was swapped mid-run. <code>modelsUsed</code> and the backgrounding-time <code>resolvedModel</code> behavior require Claude Code v2.1.212 or later.</span>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code fills <code>usage</code> and <code>totalTokens</code> from the subagent’s final API request, not from the whole run. When present, <code>thinking_tokens</code> under <code>output_tokens_details</code> in <code>usage</code> is the number of that request’s output tokens that were thinking tokens. The <code>output_tokens_details</code> key requires Python SDK v0.2.136 or later, which bundles Claude Code v2.1.228. The <code>fallback_credit</code> key requires Python SDK v0.2.162 or later, which bundles Claude Code v2.1.285.</span>

<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="monitor" aria-labelledby="_R_vb9deehkd74t9_"><a href="#monitor" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Monitor"></a><span id="_R_vb9deehkd74t9_" class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer">Monitor</span></h3>
<span data-as="p"><strong>Tool name:</strong> <code>Monitor</code></span>
<span data-as="p">Runs a background source and delivers each event to Claude so it can react without polling: <code>command</code> runs a script and emits one event per stdout line, and <code>ws</code> opens a WebSocket and emits one event per text frame. Provide exactly one of <code>command</code> or <code>ws</code>.</span>
<span data-as="p">The <code>ws</code> source requires Claude Code v2.1.195 or later. When Monitor runs a command, it follows the same permission rules as Bash. See the <a href="/docs/en/tools-reference#monitor-tool" class="link">Monitor tool reference</a> for WebSocket permissions, behavior, and provider availability.</span>

<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="error-handling" aria-labelledby="_R_17j9deehkd74t9_"><a href="#error-handling" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Error handling"></a><span id="_R_17j9deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Error handling</span></h2>

<div role="note" aria-label="Note" class="callout my-4 px-5 py-4 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl flex gap-3 border border-blue-200 bg-blue-50 dark:border-blue-900 dark:bg-blue-600/20" data-callout-type="note"><div class="mt-0.5 w-4" data-component-part="callout-icon"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="1.5" class="size-4 text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300"><use href="#mi-mint-1-CalloutNote"></use></svg></div><div class="text-sm prose dark:prose-invert min-w-0 w-full [&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-light dark:[&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-dark [&amp;_code]:text-current! [&amp;_kbd]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p">The sandbox depends on platform support and, on Linux, tools like <code>bubblewrap</code> and <code>socat</code>. By default, when <code>enabled</code> is <code>True</code> but the sandbox can’t start, commands run unsandboxed with a warning on stderr. This default differs from the TypeScript SDK, where <code>failIfUnavailable</code> defaults to <code>true</code>.</span><span data-as="p">Set <code>&quot;failIfUnavailable&quot;: True</code> in your sandbox settings to stop instead. With <code>failIfUnavailable</code> set, <code>query()</code> raises a <a href="#resulterror" class="link"><code>ResultError</code></a> when the sandbox can’t start, so wrap your <code>async for</code> loop in a <code>try</code> block. The reason is in the exception’s <code>errors</code> list. The SDK forwards <code>failIfUnavailable</code> to Claude Code along with the declared <code>SandboxSettings</code> fields.</span></div></div>
<span data-as="p">To keep sandboxed commands from writing to a file, list its absolute path under <a href="/docs/en/settings-reference#sandbox-filesystem-denywrite" class="link"><code>denyWrite</code></a> in your sandbox settings, such as <code>&quot;filesystem&quot;: {&quot;denyWrite&quot;: [&quot;/home/user/project/.env&quot;]}</code>. The SDK forwards <code>filesystem</code> to Claude Code along with the declared <code>SandboxSettings</code> fields. Once the sandbox starts, it blocks writes to each absolute path you listed.</span>

For example, allowing <code>/var/run/docker.sock</code> effectively grants full host system access through the Docker API, bypassing sandbox isolation. <h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="sandboxnetworkconfig" aria-labelledby="_R_18f9deehkd74t9_"><a href="#sandboxnetworkconfig" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: SandboxNetworkConfig"></a><span id="_R_18f9deehkd74t9_" class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>SandboxNetworkConfig</code></span></h3>

<div role="note" aria-label="Note" class="callout my-4 px-5 py-4 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl flex gap-3 border border-blue-200 bg-blue-50 dark:border-blue-900 dark:bg-blue-600/20" data-callout-type="note"><div class="mt-0.5 w-4" data-component-part="callout-icon"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="1.5" class="size-4 text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300"><use href="#mi-mint-1-CalloutNote"></use></svg></div><div class="text-sm prose dark:prose-invert min-w-0 w-full [&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-light dark:[&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-dark [&amp;_code]:text-current! [&amp;_kbd]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p">The built-in sandbox proxy enforces the network allowlist based on the requested hostname. By default, the proxy doesn’t terminate or inspect TLS traffic, so techniques such as <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domain_fronting" class="link" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">domain fronting</a> can potentially bypass the allowlist. See <a href="/docs/en/sandboxing#security-limitations" class="link">Sandboxing security limitations</a> for details and <a href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment#traffic-forwarding" class="link">Secure deployment</a> for configuring a TLS-terminating proxy.</span></div></div>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="sandboxignoreviolations" aria-labelledby="_R_18p9deehkd74t9_"><a href="#sandboxignoreviolations" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: SandboxIgnoreViolations"></a><span id="_R_18p9deehkd74t9_" class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>SandboxIgnoreViolations</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Violations to leave out of the sandbox’s violation report. Each key matches part of a command, or <code>*</code> for every command, and each value lists text to match in a violation line: <code>{&quot;*&quot;: [&quot;/etc/hosts&quot;]}</code> hides violations that mention <code>/etc/hosts</code>. A matching access is still blocked. See <a href="/docs/en/settings-reference#sandbox-ignoreviolations" class="link"><code>sandbox.ignoreViolations</code></a>.</span>

<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="permissions-fallback-for-unsandboxed-commands" aria-labelledby="_R_18v9deehkd74t9_"><a href="#permissions-fallback-for-unsandboxed-commands" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Permissions Fallback for Unsandboxed Commands"></a><span id="_R_18v9deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Permissions Fallback for Unsandboxed Commands</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">When <code>allowUnsandboxedCommands</code> is enabled, the model can request to run commands outside the sandbox by setting <code>dangerouslyDisableSandbox: True</code> in the tool input. These requests fall back to the existing permissions system, meaning your <code>can_use_tool</code> handler is invoked, allowing you to implement custom authorization logic.</span>
<span data-as="p">Your <code>excludedCommands</code> entries instead take a call out of the sandbox with no model involvement; <a href="/docs/en/settings-reference#sandbox-excludedcommands" class="link"><code>sandbox.excludedCommands</code></a> covers when an entry applies.</span>
<span data-as="p">The following example logs each unsandboxed request and denies it unless your own authorization logic allows it:</span>

<div role="note" aria-label="Warning" class="callout my-4 px-5 py-4 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl flex gap-3 border border-yellow-200 bg-yellow-50 dark:border-yellow-900 dark:bg-yellow-600/20 [&amp;_[data-component-part=&#x27;callout-icon&#x27;]]:mt-px" data-callout-type="warning"><div class="mt-0.5 w-4" data-component-part="callout-icon"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="1.5" class="flex-none size-5 text-yellow-800 dark:text-yellow-300"><use href="#mi-mint-1-CalloutWarning"></use></svg></div><div class="text-sm prose dark:prose-invert min-w-0 w-full [&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-light dark:[&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-dark [&amp;_code]:text-current! [&amp;_kbd]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-yellow-800 dark:text-yellow-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p">Commands running with <code>dangerouslyDisableSandbox: True</code> have full system access. Ensure your <code>can_use_tool</code> handler validates these requests carefully.</span><span data-as="p">If <code>permission_mode</code> is set to <code>bypassPermissions</code> and <code>allowUnsandboxedCommands</code> is enabled, the model can autonomously execute commands outside the sandbox without approval prompts, apart from the <a href="/docs/en/permission-modes#actions-no-mode-auto-approves" class="link">actions no mode auto-approves</a>. This combination effectively allows the model to escape sandbox isolation silently.</span></div></div>

If Claude Code `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/en/worktrees#isolate-subagents-with-worktrees`,children:`kept the subagent’s isolated worktree`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`worktreePath`}),` on the `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`completed`}),` variant is where to find it, and `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`worktreeBranch`}),` is its branch when Claude Code created the worktree with git.`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`On the `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`completed`}),` variant, `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`resolvedModel`}),` names the model the subagent started on, which can differ from the requested `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`model`}),` input when `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/en/model-config#restrict-model-selection`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`availableModels`})}),` or another override applies. This field requires Claude Code v2.1.174 or later. On the `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`async_launched`}),` variant, `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`resolvedModel`}),` names the model in use when the agent moved to the background, so a swap that happened before backgrounding is reflected there. The `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`modelsUsed`}),` field on both variants lists the models used in order, with consecutive repeats collapsed; it’s set only when the model was swapped mid-run. `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`modelsUsed`}),` and the backgrounding-time `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`resolvedModel`}),` behavior require Claude Code v2.1.212 or later.`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`Claude Code fills `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`usage`}),` and `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`totalTokens`}),` from the subagent’s final API request, not from the whole run. The `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`output_tokens_details`}),` key requires Python SDK v0.2.136 or later, which bundles Claude Code v2.1.228.
